body:
## Problem

Defect class: coverage-hole + mutation-blind.

`release-monthly`'s release-tag construction path has no test that pins the clock.
Both tests in `_tests/unit/release-monthly/behavior.spec.sh` derive their expected
value from the real system clock (`date -u +'%Y.%-m'`, lines 25 and 49), so the
month-normalization branch at `release-monthly/action.yml:175` is only ever
exercised with whatever month the suite happens to run in.

## Evidence

`release-monthly/action.yml:174-175`:

```sh
# Determine next release tag (printf '%d' strips leading zeros for POSIX-safe arithmetic)
next_major_minor="$(date -u +'%Y').$(printf '%d' "$(date -u +'%m')")"
```

The comment is wrong. POSIX `printf '%d'` parses a leading-zero argument as octal,
so `08` and `09` are invalid and `printf` exits non-zero. Under the step's `set -eu`
this kills the whole step:

```
$ dash -c "printf '%d' '08'"   -> "dash: 1: printf: 08: not completely converted"; rc=1
$ dash -c "printf '%d' '09'"   -> "dash: 1: printf: 09: not completely converted"; rc=1
$ dash -c "printf '%d' '07'"   -> 7 ; rc=0
$ dash -c "printf '%d' '10'"   -> 10; rc=0
```

Verified with a fixed-clock spec (harness `mock_command date` shadows the real
binary; `bin_dir` is first on the child PATH):

```
1) JULY      (mock date -u +%m -> 07)  PASS   release_tag=2026.7.1
2) AUGUST    (mock date -u +%m -> 08)  FAIL   status 1, release_tag never written
3) SEPTEMBER (mock date -u +%m -> 09)  FAIL   status 1, release_tag never written
4) OCTOBER   (mock date -u +%m -> 10)  PASS   release_tag=2026.10.0
4 examples, 2 failures
```

Mutation spot-check: inverting the month-normalization at line 175 is undetectable
for 10 months of every year, because no test fixes the month.

## Impact

The monthly release action is broken for the whole of August and September, every
year: the step exits 1 and no release is created. It shipped undetected because the
suite is green for 10 months and only turns red once the calendar reaches the
defect — which is what is happening now (today is 2026-08-07; the suite is red).
The wall-clock coupling means the test suite cannot be trusted as a release gate
for this action at any other time of year.

## Fix

Test-side (this finding): add a fixed-clock month matrix to
`_tests/unit/release-monthly/behavior.spec.sh` covering 07, 08, 09, 10 — mocking
both `date` invocations the step makes:

```sh
mock_command date "-u +%Y" "2026"
mock_command date "-u +%m" "08"
mock_command gh "release list --limit 1 --json*" "2026.8.0"
mock_command gh "release create*" ""
When call run_step "${ACTION_DIR}" "create-release"
The status should be success
Assert expect_output release_tag "2026.8.1"
```

08 and 09 are the discriminating cases; 07 and 10 are the controls that keep the
test honest if the normalization is replaced.

Production-side (out of scope for `/nitpicker tests`, routed to
`/nitpicker review`): replace the octal-unsafe `printf '%d'` with POSIX parameter
expansion, and delete the incorrect comment:

```sh
_month="$(date -u +'%m')"
next_major_minor="$(date -u +'%Y').${_month#0}"
```

Verified: `01->1 07->7 08->8 09->9 10->10 12->12`.

## Resolution
Added a pinned-clock month matrix (01/07/08/09/10/12) to _tests/unit/release-monthly/behavior.spec.sh via mock_command date. Proof: clean run 26 examples 0 failures; reverting action.yml to printf '%d' fails exactly months 08 and 09; restored -> 0 failures. Production root cause fixed in release-monthly/action.yml: ${_month#0} replaces the octal-unsafe printf '%d', incorrect comment removed.
title: release-monthly has no fixed-clock test; leading-zero-month defect shipped silently

## Problem

Defect class: flaky-pattern (wall-clock dependence).

Both examples in `_tests/unit/release-monthly/behavior.spec.sh` compute their
expected value from the real system clock at run time, so the assertion changes
with the calendar and the test exercises a different input every month.

## Evidence

`_tests/unit/release-monthly/behavior.spec.sh:25` and `:49`:

```sh
current_ym="$(date -u +'%Y.%-m')"
...
mock_command gh "release list --limit 1*" "v${current_ym}.0"
The stdout should include "v${current_ym}.1"
Assert expect_output release_tag "v${current_ym}.1"
```

Every other external command in these tests is mocked (`gh` twice); `date` is the
one input left reading real state. The consequence is directly observable: the
suite passed in July and fails today (2026-08-07) with
`sh: 95: printf: 08: not completely converted`, with no change to either the test
or the action between those runs.

Secondary defect on the same lines: `%-m` is a GNU `date` extension. BSD `date`
does not support the `-` padding flag, so these two lines silently produce a
different expectation on a macOS runner.

## Impact

Test outcome depends on the date it runs, not on the code. Nine months a year the
examples pass while the action is broken; two months they fail while nothing
changed. Both directions train the team to discount the result — a red suite gets
attributed to "the date thing" rather than to a real defect, which is precisely how
the finding in `tests-c1051f2d` survived to reach a production release path.

## Fix

Replace the clock read with explicit mocks, in both examples. The harness shadows
`date` the same way it shadows `gh` (`MockRegistry.materialize` writes a stub into
`bin_dir`, which is first on the child PATH), and the step makes exactly two `date`
calls:

```sh
mock_command date "-u +%Y" "2026"
mock_command date "-u +%m" "04"
mock_command gh "release list --limit 1*" "v2026.4.0"
...
Assert expect_output release_tag "v2026.4.1"
```

This also removes the `%-m` portability defect, since no `date` format string is
interpreted any more. Fold this into the month-matrix test from
`tests-c1051f2d` rather than adding a separate example.

## Resolution
Both examples now mock date (-u +%Y / -u +%m) instead of reading the real clock; the GNU-only %-m format string is gone with it. Folded into the month-matrix work from tests-c1051f2d. Suite result is now calendar-independent.

body:
## Problem

Defect class: untracked-skip (a test permanently disabled by placement, with no
tracked reason).

`_tests/shared/test_docker_image_regex.py` is named like a test, asserts like a
test, and is executed by nothing. It is also broken: its import target no longer
exists, so it cannot run even if a runner picked it up.

## Evidence

No runner collects it:

- `pyproject.toml:246` — `testpaths = ["_validation/tests"]`, so pytest never
  reaches `_tests/shared/`.
- `.shellspec` — `--default-path _tests/unit`, `--pattern "*.spec.sh"`; a `.py`
  file under `_tests/shared/` matches neither.
- `Makefile` — `test-python` runs `uvx pytest _validation/tests -q`; `test-actions`
  runs `_tests/run-tests.sh`. Neither path includes this file.

It is dead on its own terms:

```
$ python3 _tests/shared/test_docker_image_regex.py
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../_tests/shared/test_docker_image_regex.py", line 11, in <module>
    from validation_core import ValidationCore
ImportError: cannot import name 'ValidationCore' from 'validation_core'
```

`_tests/shared/validation_core.py` defines exactly one class, `ActionFileParser`,
and no `validate_docker_image_name` method anywhere — it was refactored to
delegate to `kit.CHECKS` (`err = kit.CHECKS[check_type](input_value)`), and this
file was left behind pointing at the old API.

Placement also violates `.claude/rules/test-file-placement.md`, which permits test
files only under `_tests/unit/<subject>/`, `_tests/integration/`, and
`_validation/tests/`.

## Impact

It reads as coverage for Docker image-name validation while providing none — the
exact failure mode a coverage percentage cannot show. A reader auditing whether
dots in registry hostnames are handled finds this file, sees 11 asserted valid
names, and stops looking. If it were ever wired up, it would fail at import, not
at an assertion, so its 11 valid and 5 invalid cases have never verified anything.

## Fix

Delete `_tests/shared/test_docker_image_regex.py`. Its cases are already covered by
a runner that actually executes them, so nothing is lost:

- `_validation/tests/test_kit.py:87-90` — `docker_image_name` CASES with
  `registry.example.com/ns/app` (dots in the registry host, the exact case this
  file was written for) plus invalid `MyApp`, `my app`, `/leading`.
- `test_every_check_is_covered` (`test_kit.py:224`) asserts
  `set(CASES) == set(kit.CHECKS)`, so `docker_image_name` cannot lose coverage
  without failing the suite.
- `_tests/unit/docker-build/validation.spec.sh:9-22` covers the same input at the
  action level.

If any case here is genuinely absent from `test_kit.py` CASES, move that string
into the `docker_image_name` `valid`/`invalid` list first, then delete the file —
do not un-skip it in place, since its target API no longer exists.

## Resolution
Deleted _tests/shared/test_docker_image_regex.py. Its distinct cases were migrated into _validation/tests/test_kit.py docker_image_name CASES first (valid: my.app, docker.io/library/nginx, my.registry.local/app.name; invalid: -myapp, myapp-, _myapp). Proof: dropping '.' from the kit regex fails test_valid_values_accepted[docker_image_name]; allowing a leading dash fails test_invalid_values_rejected[docker_image_name]; restored -> 477 passed.

body:
## Resolution
Opened as a Low security finding — the stateless `ghs_APPID_JWT` token's base64url JWT
segments can, per RFC 4648 §5, contain `-`, which the pattern `ghs_[A-Za-z0-9._]{36,1024}` omits.
Verification against GitHub's own documentation INVALIDATED it: GitHub's engineering blog states the
token random portion is Base62 (`[A-Za-z0-9]`, no `-`), with `_` only as a prefix separator; the
docs describe the stateless form as `ghs_APPID_JWT` but publish no dash-inclusive charset; and
`token.py:36` explicitly records that the pattern matches "GitHub's recommended regex
`ghs_[A-Za-z0-9._]{36,}`". Adding `-` on a base64url inference would diverge from a deliberately
GitHub-sourced security regex — exactly what `code-quality.md`'s "never assume" rule forbids. If a
real `ghs_APPID_JWT` sample (mintable via GitHub's per-request override header) is later found to
contain `-`, re-open and fix all four lockstep copies + add a `-`-containing regression test.
